Needs changes before merge.

The parent chain, moving side, and normal unit conversion have direct tests. All shipped machine files parse. The existing machine checks have no new callers or behavior changes.

### Requested before merge

1. `crates/post/src/machine/tree.rs:191` (also lines 192, 195 and 196): Check the result of each length conversion. With inch units, a head whose four dimensions are `1e308` parses successfully. Each dimension becomes `Some(inf)`. The input numbers are finite. `rate` checks the input, but `scale` can overflow. This breaks the finite-number rule for geometry and gives the future machine model an invalid size. Refuse overflow with the part id and key. Add a test for each affected field. Keep the existing behavior for an absent or nonpositive limit.

I reproduced this with a standalone program linked to the trial-merged library. No PR source or test was changed. The program set `body_diameter`, `body_length`, `max_tool_length`, and `max_tool_diameter` to `1e308` on head `h`, with `kinematics.default.units.length` set to `inch`.

```text
spindle: Some(SpindleBody { diameter: Some(inf), length: Some(inf) }); tool station: Some(ToolStation { max_tool_length: Some(inf), max_tool_diameter: Some(inf) })
reader returned a non-finite diameter
```

The assertion that the returned diameter is finite failed (exit 101).
